result:
Solution 2 is the only one whose derivation holds up. I checked it by scaling, and the result also agrees with what I recall of the published threshold, though I did not verify that against the paper.

The term |u|^{(N+α)/N} is exactly L²-critical for the Choquard interaction, because its mass-preserving scaling exponent is 0. So the threshold cannot come from comparing q with the mass-critical exponent (N+α+2)/N, which is what Solutions 1 and 3 do. Instead, the threshold comes from the cross term ∫(I_α * |u|^{p̄})|u|^q, with p̄ = (N+α)/N.

Under u_λ = λ^{N/2}u(λx), the cross term scales as λ^{(N p̄ + N q)/2 − N − α}. Since N p̄ = N+α, this exponent simplifies to (Nq − N − α)/2.

The kinetic energy scales as λ². The cross term competes with it when (Nq − N − α)/2 = 2, which gives q* = (N+α+4)/N.

For q below this value, spreading (λ → 0) lets the cross term beat the kinetic term. The energy then drops below the spreading level for every ε, so a ground state exists for all ε. For q at or above it, small ε loses the ground state.

This value lies below (N+α)/(N−2) exactly when α > N−4, which matches the stated hypothesis on α. That is further support for Solution 2.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
